title: Pervert Glasses Named Word of Year by Macquarie Dictionary
summary: Macquarie Dictionary names 'pervert glasses' its 2026 word of the year, beating AI-related terms 'nudify' and 'AI;DR' in annual language awards.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on November 23, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- Macquarie Dictionary selected 'pervert glasses' as 2026 word of the year, referencing AI-enabled smart glasses that secretly record.
- Runner-up terms included 'nudify' (AI tools creating fake explicit images) and 'AI;DR' (AI-generated summaries replacing human reading).
- Selection reflects growing public concern over AI privacy violations and the normalization of surveillance technology in everyday devices.


Australia's Macquarie Dictionary has selected 'pervert glasses' as its word of the year for 2026, spotlighting public anxiety over AI-enabled surveillance devices. The term refers to smart glasses equipped with cameras and AI capabilities that allow users to covertly record others without consent. The selection, officially announced today, reflects a broader cultural reckoning with privacy erosion in the age of wearable AI technology.


## What Are Pervert Glasses


The term 'pervert glasses' emerged in 2026 to describe smart eyewear products that integrate hidden cameras with AI-powered facial recognition, object detection, and real-time video streaming. Unlike conventional smart glasses designed for legitimate productivity or accessibility uses, these devices have sparked controversy for their potential misuse in voyeuristic surveillance and non-consensual recording.


The technology gained notoriety after several high-profile incidents involving covert recordings in public spaces, locker rooms, and private settings. Consumer advocacy groups have criticized manufacturers for inadequate privacy safeguards, while legislators in multiple countries have proposed restrictions on camera-equipped wearables in sensitive locations.


## AI-Related Runner-Up Terms


Macquarie Dictionary's shortlist for 2026 featured multiple AI-adjacent terms that illustrate technology's linguistic impact. 'Nudify' placed second, referring to AI applications that generate fake explicit images by digitally removing clothing from photographs of real people. The term has become synonymous with deepfake abuse and image-based harassment.


Third place went to 'AI;DR', a play on the internet abbreviation 'TL;DR' (too long, didn't read). The term describes AI-generated summaries that replace human reading and comprehension, raising questions about information literacy and critical thinking in an era of automated content digestion.


- Pervert glasses: Smart eyewear with covert recording capabilities
- Nudify: AI tools creating non-consensual explicit imagery
- AI;DR: Automated summaries replacing human engagement with text


## Release Date and Selection Process


Officially announced on November 23, 2026, the Macquarie Dictionary word of the year selection draws from submissions by linguists, journalists, and the Australian public throughout the calendar year. The committee evaluates terms based on cultural significance, frequency of use, and relevance to contemporary social issues.


This year's decision marks the first time a technology-related privacy concern has topped the annual list, overtaking previous winners that focused on climate, politics, and social movements. The dictionary's editorial team noted that all three finalists reflected public unease with AI's expanding role in daily life.


## What This Means


The selection of 'pervert glasses' as word of the year signals a turning point in public discourse around wearable AI. While previous years celebrated technological innovation, 2026's choice foregrounds the darker implications of ambient computing and invisible surveillance. The linguistic recognition validates growing calls for stronger privacy protections, transparent AI development, and ethical frameworks governing consumer technology. As AI capabilities become embedded in everyday objects, the vocabulary of resistance and critique is evolving alongside the technology itself.
